description: Persistent frequency and urgency, in a patient with a history of neurogenic bladder and history of stroke.
transcription: HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:  ,This is a 55-year-old female with a history of stroke, who presents today for followup of frequency and urgency with urge incontinence.  This has been progressively worsening, and previously on VESIcare with no improvement.  She continues to take Enablex 50 mg and has not noted any improvement of her symptoms.  The nursing home did not do a voiding diary.  She is accompanied by her power of attorney.  No dysuria, gross hematuria, fever or chills.  No bowel issues and does use several Depends a day.,Recent urodynamics in April 2008, here in the office, revealed significant detrusor instability with involuntary urinary incontinence and low bladder volumes, and cystoscopy was unremarkable.,IMPRESSION:  ,Persistent frequency and urgency, in a patient with a history of neurogenic bladder and history of stroke.  This has not improved on VESIcare as well as Enablex.  Options are discussed.,We discussed other options of pelvic floor rehabilitation, InterStim by Dr. X, as well as more invasive procedure.  The patient and the power of attorney would like him to proceed with meeting Dr. X to discuss InterStim, which was briefly reviewed here today and brochure for this is provided today.  Prior to discussion, the nursing home will do an extensive voiding diary for one week, while she is on Enablex, and if this reveals no improvement, the patient will be started on Ventura twice daily and prescription is provided.  They will see Dr. X with a prior voiding diary, which is again discussed.  All questions answered.,PLAN:,  As above, the patient will be scheduled to meet with Dr. X to discuss option of InterStim, and will be accompanied by her power of attorney.  In the meantime, Sanctura prescription is provided, and voiding diaries are provided.  All questions answered.

explanation: You are a 55-year-old female with a history of stroke. You also have a history of neurogenic bladder (bladder control problems caused by nerve damage). You came in for a follow-up for urinary frequency (needing to urinate often). You also have urgency (a sudden, strong need to urinate) and urge incontinence (accidental urine leakage). Your symptoms have been getting worse. You use several Depends each day. You do not have dysuria (painful urination) or gross hematuria (visible blood in your urine). You do not have a fever, chills, or bowel issues. Your power of attorney came to the visit with you. You previously took VESIcare with no improvement. You currently take Enablex 50 mg, but your symptoms have not improved. The nursing home did not complete a voiding diary (a record of urination). In April 2008, you had office urodynamics (bladder function testing). This showed significant detrusor instability (uncontrolled bladder muscle contractions). It also showed involuntary urine leakage and low bladder volumes. Your cystoscopy (a scope exam inside your bladder) was unremarkable (normal). Your doctor discussed treatment options with you and your power of attorney. Options included pelvic floor rehabilitation (pelvic muscle therapy). Another option was InterStim (a nerve stimulation procedure) with Dr. X. A more invasive procedure was also discussed. You and your power of attorney chose to meet with Dr. X to discuss InterStim. You received an information brochure about InterStim today. First, the nursing home will keep an extensive voiding diary for one week while you take Enablex. If your symptoms do not improve, you will start taking a new prescription twice daily. The text names this drug as Ventura in one section and Sanctura in another section. You will meet with Dr. X with your voiding diary and your power of attorney. All of your questions were answered.
